channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-09
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 115 news received.

item.title: 1. Nvidia CEO faces accusations linked to a possible spy
item.description: Why it matters: The investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, amid alleged Chinese espionage links and congressional scrutiny, creates significant governance, geopolitical and market risks for the most important company in AI infrastructure. Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom U.S. intelligence services reportedly suspect of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia has launched an independent investigation, and Congress is asking him to schedule a closed-door briefing.

item.title: 2. OpenAI reportedly raises $11 billion at a $1,250 billion valuation
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s reported $11 billion fundraising at a $1.25 trillion valuation highlights both the extraordinary capital demands of frontier AI and growing investor scrutiny of its path to profitability. OpenAI has reportedly secured $11 billion in a funding round that could reach $20 billion, valuing the company at $1,250 billion. The deal, more modest than expected, comes amid increased scrutiny of infrastructure spending and AI profitability.

item.title: 3. American voters reject data center projects
item.description: Why it matters: Voter opposition to data centers shows that electricity, infrastructure and community acceptance may become binding constraints on AI expansion, forcing companies such as OpenAI to offer greater economic benefits locally. In Alhambra, California, 83% of voters supported banning data centers, while in Wells, Maine, 82% approved a 180-day pause. OpenAI now proposes paying for electricity and infrastructure, publishing more information, and investing locally to win residents’ support.

item.title: 4. Coding agents fail at nearly three out of four real-world tasks
item.description: Why it matters: Real-world coding benchmarks showing leading agents fully solve only about one in four tasks challenge inflated capability claims and should materially affect enterprise deployment and investment decisions. Alibaba’s Co-Design Bench benchmark, based on real user requests, shows that GPT-6 Astra fully solves only 26.4% of tasks. Yet the same models score more than 99% on older benchmarks.

item.title: 5. Companies Remain Responsible for Their AI Agents’ Mistakes
item.description: Why it matters: UK regulators’ warning that companies remain legally responsible for autonomous agents’ mistakes establishes a crucial principle for AI governance, compliance and enterprise risk management. Four UK regulatory authorities have warned that organizations remain responsible for the autonomous AI agents they deploy.
